title: The respective roles of judge and jury
shortTitle: The respective roles of judge and jury
summary: The judge determines governing law and whether the evidence meets legal sufficiency requirements; the jury generally decides genuinely disputed facts, credibility, and the weight of evidence in a jury case. The allocation can also become a federal-state question.
notes: The assigned cases do not make every issue a jury question or permit the judge to resolve every fact labeled procedural. The source and nature of the issue matter.

sections.Meaning: The judge determines governing law and whether the evidence meets legal sufficiency requirements; the jury generally decides genuinely disputed facts, credibility, and the weight of evidence in a jury case. The allocation can also become a federal-state question.
sections.How to work through the question: Specify whether the dispute concerns sufficiency to reach a jury, the trial standard, or which decision-maker should determine a particular issue. Compare the summary-judgment cases with Byrd and Dice.
